entries.name: Slovak
entries.definition: A West Slavic language, the official language of Slovakia.

entries.name: Slovene
entries.definition: A South Slavic language spoken mainly in Slovenia.

entries.name: Smalltalk
entries.definition: A pure object-oriented programming language and environment developed at Xerox PARC in the 1970s.

entries.name: Sogdian
entries.definition: An extinct Eastern Iranian language that served as a trade language along the Silk Road.

entries.name: Somali
entries.definition: A Cushitic language, the official language of Somalia.

entries.name: Spanish
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken in Spain, Latin America and many other countries.

entries.name: SQL
entries.definition: Expressing database queries and data operations in SQL.

entries.name: Sumerian
entries.definition: An extinct language of ancient Mesopotamia, written in cuneiform and known from clay tablets.

entries.name: Sundanese
entries.definition: An Austronesian language spoken by the Sundanese people in West Java, Indonesia.

entries.name: Swabian German
entries.definition: An Alemannic dialect of German spoken in Swabia, in the southwest of Germany.

entries.name: Swahili
entries.definition: A Bantu language widely used as a lingua franca in East Africa.

entries.name: Swati
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken in Eswatini and South Africa, also called siSwati or Swazi.

entries.name: Swedish
entries.definition: A North Germanic language, the main language of Sweden and an official language of Finland.

entries.name: Swift
entries.definition: The Swift programming language; the bare label is context-sensitive.

entries.name: SystemVerilog
entries.definition: A hardware description and verification language, built as an extension of Verilog, used to design and test digital circuits.

entries.name: Tajik
entries.definition: A variety of Persian, the official language of Tajikistan.

entries.name: Tamil
entries.definition: A Dravidian language spoken mainly in Tamil Nadu in India, in Sri Lanka and in Singapore.

entries.name: Tatar
entries.definition: A Turkic language spoken mainly in Tatarstan and other parts of Russia.

entries.name: Tcl
entries.definition: A dynamic scripting language, short for Tool Command Language, created by John Ousterhout.

entries.name: Telugu
entries.definition: A Dravidian language spoken mainly in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

entries.name: Thai
entries.definition: A Kra-Dai language, the official language of Thailand.

entries.name: Tharu
entries.definition: A group of Indo-Aryan languages spoken by the Tharu people of the Terai in Nepal and northern India.

entries.name: Tibetan
entries.definition: A Sino-Tibetan language spoken mainly on the Tibetan Plateau and written in the Tibetan script.

entries.name: Tigrinya
entries.definition: A Semitic language spoken in Eritrea and the Tigray region of Ethiopia.

entries.name: Tswana
entries.definition: A Bantu language, the national language of Botswana and one of the official languages of South Africa.

entries.name: Tulu
entries.definition: A Dravidian language spoken mainly in coastal Karnataka and northern Kerala, India.

entries.name: Turkish
entries.definition: A Turkic language spoken mainly in Turkey and Cyprus, and the official language of Turkey.

entries.name: Turkmen
entries.definition: A Turkic language, the official language of Turkmenistan.

entries.name: TypeScript
entries.definition: Writing typed JavaScript programs with TypeScript.

entries.name: U-SQL
entries.definition: A Microsoft query language that combines SQL-like syntax with C# expressions, designed for large-scale data processing in Azure Data Lake Analytics.

entries.name: Ukrainian
entries.definition: An East Slavic language, the official language of Ukraine.

entries.name: UML
entries.definition: A language for modeling software systems.

entries.name: UnityScript
entries.definition: A JavaScript-like scripting language that was used to write scripts for the Unity game engine and has since been removed from it.

entries.name: Urdu
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language, the national language of Pakistan and one of the official languages of India.

entries.name: Uyghur
entries.definition: A Turkic language spoken mainly by the Uyghur people in Xinjiang, China.

entries.name: Uzbek
entries.definition: A Turkic language, the official language of Uzbekistan.

entries.name: Verilog
entries.definition: A hardware description language used to model, simulate and design digital electronic circuits.

entries.name: VHDL
entries.definition: A hardware description language, standardized by the IEEE, used to model and design digital circuits; the name abbreviates VHSIC Hardware Description Language.

entries.name: Vietnamese
entries.definition: An Austroasiatic language, the official language of Vietnam.

entries.name: Visual Basic for Applications
entries.definition: The Visual Basic-based scripting language built into Microsoft Office applications, used to automate tasks.
